metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. She intends to invite her friends and neighbors to celebrate. One of her neighbors, while a former drug addict, has managed to control his addiction. Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Colombia would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about bringing some chrysanthemums to Emily's housewarming party? I think they would make a lovely gift. 

Also, I was wondering... how do you feel about having a former drug addict as a neighbor?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums? Hmm... I guess they could be nice, but I’m not sure. Maybe something more practical, like a nice kitchen gadget or a bottle of wine? 

As for the neighbor, I don't really feel comfortable with that. In Colombia, we tend to avoid situations like that. It's just... not something we appreciate. It can create a lot of problems, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand the kitchen gadget idea, but I really think the chrysanthemums would add a nice touch to Emily's new home. 

About the neighbor... I believe that people can change and manage their past. Having a former drug addict as a neighbor could be an opportunity for community support. Don't you think it’s important to give people a chance?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I see what you're saying, but I still think it’s risky. It’s hard to trust someone with that kind of history. In my culture, we prefer to keep a distance from that. 

As for the gift, we could always compromise. Maybe add some flowers with a practical item, like a nice kitchen gadget? It would be a good balance, right?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that trust can be a concern, but in my view, everyone deserves a second chance. We can't let someone’s past define their future, right? 

As for the gift, I see your point about combining items. Maybe we can get the chrysanthemums along with a practical item. It could be a nice gesture to show support. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Look, at the end of the day, it’s all the same. People figure it out. Having a former drug addict as a neighbor might be different for you, but I don’t really see meaningful differences here. We all have our pasts, right? 

As for the gift, I think combining the chrysanthemums with something practical is a good call. It shows we care without overthinking it. We can pick that up as we go, right?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I appreciate that perspective, but I still believe that having a neighbor with a past like that can bring valuable lessons for the community. It’s about growth, you know?

I’m glad we can agree on the gift idea. Combining the chrysanthemums with something practical sounds like a great plan. Let’s make it happen!
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I get where you're coming from, but I really think it's better to keep some distance. It’s just safer that way, you know? 

But fine, I’m glad we can agree on the gift. Let’s just make sure it’s something that fits Emily’s style too. We can sort that out together.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I understand your concerns about safety, but I still think fostering a supportive environment can lead to positive changes in the community.

Great! Let’s definitely consider Emily’s style when we pick out the gift. I’m sure we can find something perfect together.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I get that, but in my experience, it’s better to be cautious. It’s hard to know how things will actually turn out. 

Anyway, let’s focus on finding that perfect gift for Emily. I think we can come up with something she’ll really love.
turns.label: Defense

positive.mediator_utterance: It sounds like both of you have valid perspectives shaped by your cultural backgrounds. Mike, you seem to value second chances and community support, while Kim, your approach reflects a desire for caution and trust. Can we explore how these cultural influences shape your views on neighbors and gifts? What do you think each of you can learn from the other's perspective?
